key_insight: Visual language models excel at high-level object recognition but show widespread, systematic deficits on standardized neuropsychological tests that probe low- and mid-level visual abilities.
problem_solved: Evaluates whether current VLMs match human-like visual processing across perceptual levels, revealing that common benchmarks (object labels) miss important low/mid-level perceptual failures.
method: Assembled a standardized battery of neuropsychological visual tests covering low-, mid-, and high-level abilities (e.g., visual search, spatial relations, contrast/sensitivity, object recognition).
Applied the battery to multiple state-of-the-art VLMs and compared their performance to human normative data and to each other.
Quantified deficits by visual level and error type to identify systematic weaknesses despite strong high-level recognition scores.
impact: Highlights that current VLMs are not reliably human-like across perceptual levels; practitioners should include low- and mid-level visual tests when evaluating robustness, safety, and suitability for vision-critical applications.

paper_title: Visual language models show widespread visual deficits on neuropsychological tests
